geos.label: South Bay
geos.blurb: San Jose, Saratoga, Sunnyvale, Mountain View

meta.standfirst: Arts, music, and worthwhile oddities, ordered by remove from Mountain View.

events.title: San Francisco 49ers vs Washington Commanders
events.note: Monday night football in the brief's home region, listed for completeness rather than recommended — the brief deprioritises stadiums and this one is a long way from cheap or walkable.

events.title: Dinosaur Jr. with Stef Chura
events.note: J Mascis at conversational volume is still the loudest thing on the Peninsula this week — three-chord melody buried under a wall of Marshall fuzz, forty years in and unreformed. A 500-cap room is an absurdly small place to hear it.

events.title: Japanese Tea Garden free admission hour
events.venue: Japanese Tea Garden, Golden Gate Park
events.note: The oldest public Japanese garden in the country, free for the first hour on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays. Non-residents otherwise pay $12-16; San Francisco residents are always free with ID.

events.title: Matinee: Lesser Care + Rotten Charms
events.note: A five o'clock darkwave matinee, which is a sentence that only makes sense at this bar. Lesser Care do the cold, reverbed end of post-punk properly.

events.title: SF Politics 101
events.note: SPUR's plain-language explainer of how the city is actually governed — charter, commissions, where the money goes. Free, and more useful than most paid civics.

events.title: SalsaCrazy Mondays
events.note: Lessons at half six, dancing after, and the floor stays busy until midnight on a weeknight. Ten dollars if you skip the class.

events.title: Dirty Mondays: Pinfall, Driver Coaster, Nothing Special, A Dream About Home
events.note: Four local bands for nothing on a Monday in a Mission bar. Unticketed, which is why no aggregator carries it — this listing exists because the venue's DICE calendar was read directly.

events.title: Motown on Mondays
events.note: Fifteen years of the same idea done well: soul 45s, all night, free before eight and five dollars after. The longest-running weekly in the Divisadero corridor.

events.title: Hayes Valley Comedy Night
events.note: Free with an RSVP, twenty to twenty-five at the door, two-drink minimum. A standing Monday that is reliably better than free comedy has any right to be.

events.title: Open Mic Night
events.note: The oldest open mic in the city, in a saloon that predates the 1906 fire. Sign-up early; the list is long and the stage is small.

events.title: almost monday with Rec Hall
events.note: San Diego trio making bright, major-key surf-pop that sounds engineered for a car advert and is better than that implies. Doors seven.

events.title: Hovvdy with Emma Ogier
events.note: Austin duo working the quietest end of American indie — two acoustic guitars, close harmony, drum machines kept low. Ten years of it now and they have got better at the restraint, not worse.

events.title: NEW CONSTELLATIONS with Vox Rea
events.note: Sold out before the week began. The touring version of a travelling arts-and-conversation project rather than a straight gig, which is why it went so fast.

events.title: Bebe Stockwell with Khatumu
events.note: Early-career singer-songwriter on a Monday, which is what the Rickshaw is for. All ages.

events.title: DJ X'ces with Turbo Sonidero, Grupo Gallardo, Sonido Aztlan
events.note: Sonidero night in the old Barbary Coast hall — cumbia records pitched down and stretched out through a sound system, with Turbo Sonidero's digital rebuilds of the form alongside the traditional selectors. The best Monday dance in the city.

events.title: Krazy for Karaoke
events.note: The Monday fixture, nine until close, free.

events.title: Julian Lage Quartet with Laura Itandehui
events.note: Lage plays jazz guitar with the touch of a chamber musician and the repertoire instincts of a folk player, and the quartet with John Medeski on organ is the loosest version of the band. He does this again at Stanford on Wednesday; the Davies room is the bigger occasion, the Bing the better listen.

events.title: Post Sex Nachos with Hannah Geller
events.note: Jangly Midwestern guitar pop with a band name designed to be unforgettable and unsayable. The basement room suits them better than the name suggests.

events.title: Spencer Krug with Emory Duncan
events.note: The voice and the piano behind Wolf Parade and Sunset Rubdown, solo and seated in a wood-panelled hall built by a fraternal order. Krug's songs were always too strange for the rooms they got; this is the right one.

events.title: Grupo Ju-Juy and Grupo Kl de Edwin Zacary
events.note: Regional Mexican bill at the Mission nightclub; found only through the ticketing sweep, so the billing order may not be the room's.

events.title: Yoon Chung Han: Dreaming Babies: illi (closing day)
events.note: Last day of Han's installation, which turns biometric data into generative sound and image. Gray Area publishes no gallery hours on its events page; the closing date is the one hard fact it gives.

events.title: Town Biz Comedy Night with HellaFunny
events.note: Free with RSVP in a Fruitvale mezcaleria. HellaFunny run the best free comedy circuit in the East Bay and this is the Monday end of it.

events.title: Free Solo Theater: Untold Stories of America's Dreamers
events.note: Shotgun Players' home stage, given over to solo work about immigration and DACA. Sliding-scale donation and free at the door, which is unusual for anything this side of a reading.

events.title: Geese with Bill Orcutt
events.note: Both Oakland nights sold out. Geese have mutated from Brooklyn post-punk kids into something closer to a jam band with a theatre-kid frontman, and Cameron Winter's voice is the reason. Bill Orcutt opening — solo electric guitar at its most abrasive and least accommodating — is one of the best support bookings of the year.

events.title: Bobby McFerrin
events.note: A ten-time Grammy winner in a 600-seat listening room, improvising with his voice as a whole band. McFerrin at this scale is a much stranger and better proposition than the one song everyone knows.

events.title: Shoshana Bean
events.note: Broadway belter working the cabaret-with-a-rhythm-section format. Big voice, small room.

events.title: The Jerry Douglas Band
events.note: The most recorded dobro player alive, and the one who moved the instrument out of bluegrass orthodoxy and into something closer to jazz phrasing. Fourteen Grammys. Doors half six.

events.title: Walking Tour: Cityscapes & Public Spaces
events.note: Two hours on downtown's privately owned public spaces and the rules that produced them. Free.

events.title: Civic Center Soundtrack
events.note: Free lunchtime music and food trucks on the library side of Civic Center, Tuesdays and Thursdays. A small programme doing more for that plaza than any amount of policing has.

events.title: Pop-up Double Dutch Jump Rope
events.note: Two hours of double dutch on a downtown plaza at lunchtime, free, no skill assumed. The sort of thing the Financial District does not usually get.

events.title: Tear Dungeon, Shy Lobby and Mars Occult
events.note: Early doors at six for three local bands at the noisy end. Read off the venue's ticketing widget; nothing else carries it.

events.title: Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde (1931)
events.note: Rouben Mamoulian's pre-Code version, with Fredric March's transformations done in-camera through coloured filters and makeup. Still the best of the adaptations.

events.title: Arthouse50: A Barbara Hammer Tribute
events.note: Hammer made the foundational body of lesbian experimental film in the Bay Area in the 1970s. Part of the Arthouse 50 series.

events.title: 826 Valencia's Writer's Block Party
events.note: Fundraiser for the Mission writing centre, 21+, and the ticket covers the beer and wine. $40.

events.title: Live Model Tuesday Sketch
events.note: Bring your own paper. A life-drawing session in a bar, which is exactly as sociable and as serious as that sounds.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: The Mischief company's wreck-the-pantomime formula, running at the Playhouse until the end of November. Physical comedy executed with the precision of a stunt sequence. Tuesday is the cheap night of the week.

events.title: Oh, Mary!
events.note: Cole Escola's Mary Todd Lincoln as a thwarted cabaret diva, eighty minutes, no interval, and the funniest thing to come off Broadway in years. A.C.T. publishes no curtain times anywhere on its site, so this time comes from ticket resellers and is the honest best available.

events.title: Litquake: Alain Damasio, Horde of the Counterwind
events.note: The French science-fiction novelist whose best-known book has only just been translated into English, in a small North Beach bookshop. Free, with a $10-15 suggested donation.

events.title: Litquake: Brian Evenson
events.note: Evenson writes short horror fiction with the sentences filed down to nothing, and he is one of the few writers whose work is genuinely improved by being read aloud.

events.title: Mad Props: A Comedy Breakdown of the California Ballot
events.note: KALW get comedians to read the ballot propositions so you do not have to. Free, and genuinely the most efficient way to arrive at an informed vote.

events.title: The Ring: film with live orchestra
events.note: Verbinski's 2002 remake with Hans Zimmer's score played live by the San Francisco Symphony. The score is mostly texture rather than tune, which makes it a genuinely odd thing to watch an orchestra produce. From $69.

events.title: Hayes Valley Comedy Night
events.note: Free with RSVP, two-drink minimum.

events.title: Shakey Graves with Wild Pink
events.note: Alejandro Rose-Garcia's one-man-band act grew into a real band some years ago and the songs got better for it. Wild Pink's open-hearted heartland rock is the right opener.

events.title: Allah-Las with April Magazine
events.note: Los Angeles band who have made the same sun-bleached sixties garage record five or six times and are very good at it. San Francisco's own April Magazine open with something hazier and more damaged.

events.title: The Devil Makes Three with Two Runner
events.note: First of two nights. Santa Cruz-formed trio playing ragtime, country blues and murder ballads with no drummer and a lot of forward momentum. Two Runner are the best new old-time duo in the state.

events.title: Tōth with Sean Nicholas Savage
events.note: Alex Toth left Rubblebucket's horn section to make quieter, sadder records under his own name. Sean Nicholas Savage opening is the wild card — lounge-pop sung with total sincerity and no irony at all.

events.title: Sawyer Hill with Never Ending Fall
events.note: Young songwriter on a first proper headline run.

events.title: Avery Cochrane with Karly Bowman
events.note: All ages, doors at seven.

events.title: Copeathetic with Scissoring, Half Calf and Closegood
events.note: Four-band local bill, eight o'clock.

events.title: Lost Highway
events.note: Lynch's least-loved and most genuinely unnerving nineties film. Robert Blake's Mystery Man scene has not got less frightening.

events.title: This Is Buzz, with Mark Pellington Q&A
events.note: Documentary with the director in the room afterwards.

events.title: Kilowatt Karaoke
events.note: Nine o'clock, Tuesdays, and busier than most Mission bands manage.

events.title: Laura Veirs and Karl Blau
events.note: Veirs writes plain-spoken songs about weather, geology and marriage and sings them in a voice that never oversells. Karl Blau's countrypolitan baritone is a real pairing, not a warm-up.

events.title: ARTMS
events.note: Five of the former LOONA members, reconstituted after a long contract fight, and one of the more interesting things in K-pop because the group effectively owns its own narrative now.

events.title: Drift Mothership, Manifestiv and Big Empty Zero
events.note: The only touring concert either DNA mirror carries this week, and the club's own calendar would not load. Psych-leaning local bill; see Thin this week for what is missing.

events.title: Pumpkin Paints: Pots + Pints for Ruth Bancroft Garden
events.note: Benefit for the Walnut Creek dry garden, which is one of the great plant collections in the state and chronically short of money. $30.

events.title: Mezcal & Mole Comedy Night
events.note: Free with RSVP, Tuesdays.

events.title: Litquake: Memoirs, Writing Against Silence or Erasure
events.note: Panel on memoir as a response to being written out of the record. Free.

events.title: Twin Peaks: Conversation with the Stars
events.note: Cast panel rather than a concert, which is why it is priced like one. $70-99.

events.title: Geese with Bill Orcutt
events.note: Second of two sold-out nights. See Monday — and if you have a ticket for only one, Orcutt's support slot is the reason to arrive early.

events.title: $6 Drive-In Movie Night
events.note: Six dollars a head, two dollars for children, two screens, Tuesdays only. One of two surviving drive-ins in the region and the cheapest film in this digest.

events.title: Engelbert Humperdinck
events.note: Ninety years old and still touring a repertoire of 1960s easy-listening hits in a restored 1927 movie palace. A legacy act in the literal sense; the building is half the draw.

events.title: Dracula (TheatreWorks Silicon Valley)
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: TheatreWorks' autumn mainstage, running to 1 November. Tonight's performance has a post-show discussion with the cast — the company does these on Wednesdays and they are open to anyone with a ticket.

events.title: Bo Johnson
events.note: Midweek headline slot at the downtown club.

events.title: Roosters Comedy Showcase
events.note: The club's own Wednesday showcase — a rotating bill of local comics, no headliner announced. Cheaper than the weekend and the room is the same.

events.title: Taste of Filoli Tour
events.note: Ninety minutes in the garden with honey and jam tasting and a Chase Wines pour at the end.

events.title: Bat Week Screening: The Invisible Mammal
events.note: Documentary on North American bats and white-nose syndrome, in a municipal rec centre, free. Exactly the sort of civic programming the brief says gets missed.

events.title: Julian Lage Quartet with John Medeski, Jorge Roeder and Kenny Wollesen
events.note: The same quartet that plays Davies on Monday, in a hall built for acoustic detail — Medeski's organ and Wollesen's cymbals are the parts that benefit. Laura Itandehui opens. The better of the two nights if you care about hearing it rather than being there.

events.title: Free Admission Wednesday
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: Galleries free every Wednesday, 11am to 8pm — Rael San Fratello's architectural prototypes, GaHee Park's paintings and Dread Scott's The Body Politic are all up. The free day is the point and the late closing makes it workable after work.

events.title: Biblio Bistro Farmers' Market Cooking School
events.note: Free cooking demonstration at the Heart of the City farmers' market, built around whatever is on the stalls that morning.

events.title: Jazz on the Plaz(a) with Jazz Mafia: season finale
events.note: Last of the season. Jazz Mafia are the collective that has done more than anyone to keep live brass in San Francisco's public spaces. Free, lunchtime, outdoors.

events.title: Free Art Workshop: Halloween Garland
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: Two hours in the Grand Lobby, free with registration, materials provided.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong (matinee)
events.note: The Wednesday matinee, two o'clock. The only daytime performance midweek.

events.title: Rocky Horror Picture Show with a full shadow cast
events.note: A shadow cast, in a public library, for free. Space is limited and it will go; get there well before five.

events.title: Kanal (4K restoration)
events.note: Wajda's 1957 film of the Warsaw Uprising fought out in the sewers. Restored, and still one of the bleakest war films ever made.

events.title: Litquake: Artificial Intimacy, Sherry Turkle on AI
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: Turkle has been writing about what machines do to human relationships since the early eighties, which makes her the least hysterical and most useful person to hear on this subject. Advance tickets gone; limited walk-ins at the door, which open at five.

events.title: APAture Literary Showcase
events.note: Kearny Street Workshop's annual festival of emerging Asian Pacific American artists, literary night. Recovered from a search index rather than a calendar, so the price is unconfirmed.

events.title: NAZA
events.note: In its second week at the Roxie and showing most days.

events.title: Chipped Nail Polish, Andrew St. James and Woodpecker Dynamite
events.note: Andrew St. James has been one of the better San Francisco songwriters for a decade without ever quite leaving. Seven o'clock.

events.title: Litquake: California Journeys
events.note: Free reading at the public radio station. One of the handful of Litquake events this run could actually confirm.

events.title: Astronomy Lecture: Living with the Stars on the Day of the Dead
events.note: Free lecture at the Corona Heights museum, pitched at adults rather than children for once.

events.title: Free Public Rooftop Stargazing
events.note: The university opens its roof and its large telescope to the public on October Wednesdays and Fridays, free. Weather-dependent, which in the Sunset means check before you go.

events.title: Assimilation (Word for Word)
events.note: Word for Word stage short stories without cutting a sentence, narration included, which sounds like a gimmick until you watch it work. Running to 8 November.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Evening performance, seven o'clock.

events.title: Manon (San Francisco Opera)
events.note: Massenet's Manon, the second of four remaining performances. From $30, which for this house is the cheapest serious music in the city.

events.title: DIIV with Pink Breath of Heaven
events.note: Zachary Cole Smith's band have spent a decade getting heavier and slower, and the current record is closer to shoegaze-as-doom than to the jangly thing they started as. Loud room, loud band.

events.title: Todd Rundgren: Damned If I Do Tour
events.note: An evening with — no support, long set. Rundgren wrote some of the best pop singles of the seventies and then spent fifty years refusing to be a pop act, and the show is usually both of those things at once.

events.title: The Devil Makes Three with Two Runner
events.note: Second night. The Tuesday will have sold the better seats; the Wednesday crowd is usually the one that knows the deep cuts.

events.title: Kylie Cantrall with GIRLSET
events.note: Disney Channel graduate making straightforward dance-pop, playing a room much bigger than the songs need. The audience will be young and extremely loud.

events.title: Yana: The Feelings Are Forever Tour
events.note: Sold out. All ages, doors at seven.

events.title: Madrone is 22!
events.note: The Divisadero bar's own birthday, which in practice means a full night of its resident DJs and no cover.

events.title: Nerd Nite SF #165
events.note: Three talks, three beers, no slide discipline. A hundred and sixty-five editions in and still the cheapest intellectual night in the city at $10-15.

events.title: The Big Picture
events.note: A one-night limited engagement in A.C.T.'s main house, doors seven for an eight o'clock start — and the only performance all week at either of A.C.T.'s own theatres that carries a published time.

events.title: All Hallows Eve: An Evening with Ellen Datlow & Friends
events.note: Datlow has edited the best horror anthologies in English for forty years. $15, in a fifty-seat room, which is the right scale for being read to in the dark.

events.title: Gialloween VI: Dario Argento's Door Into Darkness
events.note: Argento's early television anthology, which is where a lot of the giallo grammar got worked out before the features. Sixth year of the Roxie's Gialloween series.

events.title: Even Just
events.note: New independent feature, one show.

events.title: Metal Box Dance Party with DJ Mo'Ski
events.note: Post-punk and industrial records, named after the Public Image Ltd album, which tells you the selection.

events.title: Gnash with Salem Ilise and Brake
events.note: The bedroom-pop confessional act that had an enormous 2016 single and has been quietly making records since. Note that August Hall lists him again on Thursday; both are the venues' own calendars and only two nights in the same city explains it.

events.title: City of the Sun
events.note: Instrumental trio — two guitars and percussion, flamenco technique applied to post-rock structures. Listed on the ticketing sweep but absent from the venue's own calendar, so treat the date as unconfirmed.

events.title: Nahko and Medicine for the People
events.note: From the ticketing sweep only — The Great Northern's own page carries no dates at all, as it has not for months.

events.title: Deep House Yoga
events.note: Yoga class on the main floor of a nightclub with a DJ instead of a playlist. More fun than it sounds and the only daytime use that room gets.

events.title: Patch Bay: From Lore to Logic
events.note: Gray Area's workshop strand, on building interactive worlds. The only in-person thing on their calendar this week — the Yoon Chung Han exhibition closes on the 19th.

events.title: Oakland Museum of California galleries
events.note: Open Wednesday to Sunday. Black Power, BeHere / 1942 on the Japanese American incarceration, and You Are Here on California map-making are all up, and the Panther archive material that drew crowds for the sixtieth is still on view.

events.title: Bay St Sunset Market Car Show
events.note: Free evening market with a car show attached.

events.title: Profs & Pints Alameda: Faith and Frights
events.note: An academic on religion and horror, in a brewery on the old naval air station. $13.50 in advance.

events.title: Glue Stick Social: Junk Journaling by the Glow of a Creepy Picture Show
events.note: Collage and scrapbooking in a West Oakland church with a horror film running silently behind it. Free, and the best-named event of the week.

events.title: Marjorie Keller Films
events.note: Keller's diaristic 16mm work, which sits alongside Hammer's in the American experimental canon and gets shown a fraction as often.

events.title: Malcolm Todd with 54 Ultra
events.note: First of two sold-out nights. Twenty-one-year-old making loose, jazz-chord bedroom pop that has outgrown the bedroom entirely.

events.title: Bedouine
events.note: Azniv Korkejian writes in the Laurel Canyon idiom without ever sounding like pastiche, and her voice is low and unhurried enough to carry a seated room on its own.

events.title: Clay Aiken
events.note: $60-129 for a 400-seat room.

events.title: Matt Pond PA with Anya Marina
events.note: From the ticketing sweep; the venue keeps no calendar this run could read.

events.title: Disney On Ice: Find Your Hero
events.note: Opening night of a four-day arena run. From $35. Listed for completeness — the brief deprioritises arenas and this one is findable without help.

events.title: Switchfoot with Anberlin
events.note: Two bands from the early-2000s Christian-adjacent alternative scene, playing a hillside amphitheatre above Saratoga in late October. Bring a coat; the venue is at 2,000 feet and the shuttle queue is cold.

events.title: Dracula (TheatreWorks Silicon Valley)
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Tonight is the ASL-interpreted performance, which TheatreWorks schedules once per run and publishes properly — worth knowing because almost nobody else in the South Bay does.

events.title: Jim Henson's Labyrinth: In Concert
events.note: The 1986 film with Trevor Jones's score and the Bowie songs played live. The Henson creature work holds up better than almost any CGI of the intervening forty years.

events.title: Hablando Huevadas
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: The Peruvian stand-up double act, touring one of the biggest Spanish-language comedy shows in the Americas. Found through the venue feed rather than a presenter, so the running time is unconfirmed.

events.title: Marcus Monroe with Ben Feldman and Nick Scarpino
events.note: Juggling and stand-up in the same act, done well enough that the juggling is not the joke.

events.title: Liz Splatt
events.note: One show, eight o'clock.

events.title: Steely Dead
events.note: A Grateful Dead and Steely Dan mashup band, which is a genuinely strange premise given that the two bands agreed on almost nothing. The brief says list tributes and never feature them; this is the listing.

events.title: Walking Tour: 1840s San Francisco and the legacy of America's first Black millionaire
events.note: William Leidesdorff died in 1848 owning a large part of what is now the Financial District. Free, ninety minutes, starts where the alley is named after him.

events.title: Civic Center Soundtrack
events.note: Free lunchtime concert and food trucks.

events.title: Chess on the Plaza
events.note: Boards out at lunchtime, free, all comers.

events.title: NAZA
events.note: Afternoon show.

events.title: Frances Ancheta at the Mission Community Market
events.note: Live music at the Thursday street market on Bartlett. Free, outdoors, and the market itself is the better reason to go.

events.title: VFX Artists' Fine Art Double Feature
events.note: Visual effects artists showing the work they make when nobody is paying them. Free.

events.title: Día de los Muertos NightLife
events.note: The Thursday 21+ opening with a Day of the Dead programme — the aquarium, the rainforest dome and a planetarium, with bars. $26, last entry nine. The single best-value evening in Golden Gate Park.

events.title: SF Latino Film Festival opening night: STREET SMART, Lessons from a TV Icon
events.note: Eighteenth edition of the festival, opening with a documentary on a Spanish-language television institution. $15, and the festival runs through the weekend at the Roxie and New People.

events.title: Macabre Marvels in the Stack
events.note: The library's special collections staff bringing out the genuinely unsettling items. Free.

events.title: Bay Area Protest Photojournalists panel and pop-up exhibit
events.note: Photographers who have covered Bay Area demonstrations, with prints on the wall for the evening. Free.

events.title: Eyewitness to the Resistance
events.note: Free presentation in the Koret.

events.title: B-Movie: Lust & Sound in West-Berlin
events.note: Archive-footage documentary on the West Berlin music underground between 1979 and 1989, free at the Goethe-Institut. Essential companion viewing for anyone going to Substance Festival the same night.

events.title: Terror Vault: 1874 Halloween Haunt
events.note: Immersive haunt staged in the Old Mint's vaults, which are the genuinely frightening part. $10 off with the Funcheap code.

events.title: Live Latin Jazz: Pepe and Friends
events.note: Three hours of Latin jazz in a hotel bar with no cover.

events.title: Substance Festival 2026: A Split Second and Crash Course in Science
events.note: Opening night of a four-day darkwave and minimal-synth festival. A Split-Second's Flesh was one of the records that invented Belgian new beat, and Crash Course in Science made synth-punk out of hardware store parts in 1979. Automelodi, Vioflesh, Pink Stiletto and God Tongue fill the bill. Doors six, early start.

events.title: The Scout (open captioned)
events.note: Open-captioned screening, which the Roxie marks on its calendar and almost no other repertory house in the city does.

events.title: Faux Real, Kyra Machida and Bryce Xavier
events.note: Faux Real are two French brothers doing art-pop as performance art, and the Mission bar is an unlikely but correct setting.

events.title: Halloween Warm Up Party with Malice Cooper, Indestructible and Fast Friends
events.note: An Alice Cooper tribute called Malice Cooper, a week early, seven o'clock.

events.title: Music at Mechanics' presents New Century Chamber Orchestra
events.note: The conductorless string orchestra playing in the 1854 library on Post Street. The series is free with registration; confirmed through Downtown SF's calendar rather than the institute's own page, which a plain fetch cannot reach.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Seven o'clock.

events.title: Assimilation (Word for Word)
events.note: Thursdays at seven.

events.title: Hisaishi Conducts Hisaishi
events.note: First of three. Joe Hisaishi conducting the San Francisco Symphony in the West Coast premiere of his own Concerto for Orchestra, which the orchestra commissioned. He is known here for forty years of Miyazaki scores; this is the concert-hall composer, and he is conducting it himself. The single most consequential booking of the week and effectively sold out at face value.

events.title: Country Risqué record release, with Dinner Date, Barfight and Tom Conneely and Birds of Paradise
events.note: Local record release with three support acts for $15-20, which is the best-value bill in the city tonight. Half seven start, all ages.

events.title: HellaFunny Thursday Comedy Night
events.note: Free with RSVP.

events.title: Frankie Cosmos: 10 Years of Next Thing, with Gabby's World
events.note: Greta Kline playing the 2016 record front to back. Next Thing is the one where the two-minute songs stopped sounding like sketches and started sounding finished, and Gabby's World on support makes this a straight reunion of that scene.

events.title: George Clanton with ideasforconversations
events.note: The man who turned vaporwave from an internet joke into an actual live act, with a stage show that involves crowd-surfing more than ambient music usually does.

events.title: Justin Nozuka with Nimitt
events.note: Soft-voiced Canadian songwriter nearly twenty years into a career that never quite broke and never quite stopped.

events.title: Fabio Frizzi: FRIZZI2FULCI, with DEATHX_XHEAD
events.note: Frizzi wrote the scores for Fulci's Zombie and The Beyond, and this is him with a band playing them as music rather than as accompaniment. Progressive-rock organ, funeral choirs and a drum machine. Doors seven for an eight o'clock start, 21+.

events.title: Ghost in the Shell: 30th Anniversary Remaster
events.note: Oshii's 1995 film remastered, in the Japantown basement cinema that is the right size for it.

events.title: Filipiñana, presented by FiliKula
events.note: Golf-caddie drama from the Philippines, programmed by a local Filipino film collective.

events.title: The History of Concrete
events.note: Playing most nights this week at half eight.

events.title: MuZiek with Aaron Hammerman
events.note: Thursday residency, no cover before late.

events.title: Inner Circle Dance Party
events.note: Free with RSVP, nine o'clock.

events.title: Level Up Thursdays
events.note: Video DJ night on Folsom, free, until two.

events.title: Rise Against and Alkaline Trio
events.note: Two bands who have been co-headlining in some configuration for twenty years, on a bill that is better value than either alone. Alkaline Trio's catalogue is the deeper one.

events.title: MONSTA X
events.note: In the Theater configuration rather than the full hall. One of the harder-edged K-pop groups and one of the few still built around rap verses.

events.title: The Aquabats with Mariachi El Bronx and Mrs. Magician
events.note: A costumed superhero ska band and the Bronx's mariachi alter ego on the same bill, which is the most purely silly and best-value ticket of the week. Mariachi El Bronx are not a novelty — the arrangements are real.

events.title: The Rose Hips with Sun Casino
events.note: Local garage-pop on the basement bill.

events.title: gnash
events.note: August Hall's own calendar lists him tonight and Café du Nord's lists him on Wednesday; both are first-party pages, so either he plays twice or one is stale. No time published on either.

events.title: X CLUB.
events.note: From the ticketing sweep — 1015's own site renders its calendar client-side and returned nothing again this week.

events.title: Litquake: Chad Harbach on The Brightness
events.note: Harbach's first novel since The Art of Fielding, fifteen years on. No start time could be confirmed — Litquake's schedule is hosted on a platform that refuses this run.

events.title: DJ Cira
events.note: From the sweep; Monarch keeps no calendar this run can read.

events.title: Heavy Metal Market and Industrial Artisan Fair
events.note: Free entry to West Oakland's industrial arts school, with its makers selling the work and short workshops running alongside. Blacksmithing, neon, glass. The best market in this digest.

events.title: Breathless
events.note: Godard's 1960 first feature, in a season the museum is building around his early work — the Gvido Augusts poster exhibition upstairs is part of the same programme.

events.title: The Becomers
events.note: Independent science-fiction horror comedy in a microcinema that programmes almost nothing you can see elsewhere. $15.

events.title: POC Comedy Night
events.note: Free with RSVP, Temescal.

events.title: Storytelling Show Under the Big Top
events.venue: The Big Top at Radium Runway
events.note: Moth-format storytelling in an actual circus tent on the old naval air station. $27.45.

events.title: Malcolm Todd with 54 Ultra
events.note: Second sold-out night.

events.title: Tommy Davidson
events.note: In Living Color alumnus, $39-84, with paid meet-and-greets either side of the show. The ticketing sweep listed Rakim here tonight instead; the venue's own calendar says Davidson, and the venue wins.

events.title: Tommy Castro & the Painkillers
events.note: Bay Area blues-soul band who have been the reliable working version of that music here for thirty years.

events.title: Maria BC, Kathryn Mohr and Claire Cronin
events.note: Three songwriters working the quietest, most haunted end of the form on one bill — Maria BC's guitar tone alone is worth the ticket. The venue's own calendar fetched empty this week, so this comes from the sweep.

events.title: 5th Annual Fall Gala: An Evening with St. Vincent
events.note: Annie Clark in a 300-capacity room in Mill Valley, as the venue's annual fundraiser. She plays arenas; this is the kind of booking that happens once and then gets talked about for a decade. Doors seven. The clearest case for the drive north this digest has had all autumn.

events.title: Disney On Ice: Find Your Hero
events.note: Second night of the arena run.

events.title: UB40
events.note: The Campbell brothers' version of the band, playing the Labour of Love covers catalogue that made them the biggest reggae act in Britain. A hillside winery in October is a strange place for it and that is part of the appeal.

events.title: An Intimate Evening with Kalani Pe'a
events.venue: Carriage House Theatre, Montalvo Arts Center
events.note: Three-time Grammy winner for Hawaiian music, singing in Hawaiian and English in a 300-seat barn on the Montalvo estate. This venue only entered the digest last week and this is the first listing it has produced — the best South Bay booking of the week by some distance.

events.title: Dracula (TheatreWorks Silicon Valley)
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Friday at half seven.

events.title: Protomartyr with Accessory
events.note: Joe Casey talks rather than sings over the best post-punk rhythm section in America, and the subject is almost always Detroit. They play August Hall tomorrow; this is the smaller, better room.

events.title: Bronco
events.note: Monterrey grupero institution, fifty years in, playing a 3,000-seat hall. One of the larger Spanish-language bookings of the season here.

events.title: Kellen Erskine with Ben Feldman and Nick Scarpino
events.note: Eight o'clock.

events.title: Marlon Wayans
events.note: Five shows across the weekend, starting with the late one tonight.

events.title: K-POP x EDM with TiffVny Joy
events.note: Ten o'clock, 21+, and walkable from Caltrain Sunnyvale, which is rare for a South Bay club night.

events.title: Grupo Kachimba
events.note: Banda night; from the ticketing sweep.

events.title: Jontavious Willis (early show)
events.note: A Georgia bluesman in his twenties playing Piedmont and Delta repertoire on acoustic guitar with no revivalist self-consciousness at all. Taj Mahal called him the wunderkind and was not exaggerating. Two shows tonight in a 200-seat studio.

events.title: Jontavious Willis (late show)
events.note: Second show at nine. The late set in a room this small is the one to take.

events.title: Lower Polk Live! free music and art street festival
events.note: Polk Street closed for a free evening street festival with stages and galleries open. The best free thing on a Friday this month.

events.title: From The E: Fall Festival Night Market
events.note: Free night market in the Excelsior, which is the part of the city that gets the least of this and has the best food.

events.title: Free Outdoor Movie Night
events.note: Parkside neighbourhood screening, starts at dusk. Free.

events.title: Drunk Secretary Happy Hour
events.note: A six o'clock DJ night, which is the Knockout's particular contribution to San Francisco nightlife: a dance floor that is over before most clubs open.

events.title: In Their Name: Día de Los Muertos 2026
events.note: SOMArts' annual Day of the Dead exhibition, in its twenty-seventh year, which is the most serious ofrenda installation in the city and nothing like the street festival version. $15, free for under-sixteens.

events.title: 30th Anniversary AIDS Benefit Art Party
events.note: Free, with an optional donation, in the poster-art centre on Haight Street.

events.title: Halloween Carnival of Curiosities
events.note: A residential block closed off and turned into a free sideshow. Ingleside, six o'clock.

events.title: Lady
events.note: Two shows tonight.

events.title: Marie Antoinette (4K restoration)
events.note: Coppola's 2006 film restored, with a companion documentary on Saturday. The Converse shot still earns its place.

events.title: Take Me Home (open captioned)
events.note: Six o'clock, rush seating only.

events.title: Substance Festival 2026: TR/ST and Buzz Kull
events.note: Night two of the darkwave festival, and the strongest bill of it: TR/ST DJing, Buzz Kull, Kontravoid, Zanias, Ghost Cop, Aux Animaux and DJ Omar Perez. Doors six. Four-day passes $90-250.

events.title: Fall Friday Night Movies: Fantastic Mr. Fox
events.note: Free outdoor screening on the Mission Rock waterfront. Half six, and it will be cold.

events.title: Mala Greña and Suika T with DJ Lizzy Al Toque
events.note: Latin punk and cumbia in the front room at seven, one of four separate things this bar is running tonight.

events.title: Mr. Floyd Larry, Foliage and Badvril
events.note: Second seven o'clock bill, same night, same bar.

events.title: Big Bad Wolf Tour: live music and political power
events.note: Free for the first three hundred RSVPs — a touring organising event with bands attached. Recovered from Funcheap, not from the club, whose own calendar refuses this run by name.

events.title: Yerba Buena Illuminated: 95-foot art projection
events.note: Projected artwork up the side of the 1908 Humboldt Bank tower on Market Street, free, from seven. Mid-Market's best recent idea.

events.title: Free Public Rooftop Stargazing
events.note: Second of the week. Free, weather permitting.

events.title: Floating Features: Hocus Pocus
events.note: Part of the Roxie's Floating Features strand. Seven o'clock.

events.title: One Battle After Another, outdoors
events.note: Free screening on the Hayes Valley lot. Quarter past seven.

events.title: Hisaishi Conducts Hisaishi
events.note: Second of three nights. See Thursday — and if you are choosing, resale on the Friday is marginally less punishing than on the Thursday.

events.title: Magos Herrera and Edward Simon: Femeninas
events.note: Simon's Femeninas project — settings of Latin American women poets and composers — with Magos Herrera singing and Luis Quintero on percussion. Half seven. THE HALL IS UNCONFIRMED: the only route that reads SFJAZZ at all missed this show entirely, and it was recovered from the regional sweep, which names the building and not the room. It could be the Joe Henderson Lab.

events.title: Oh, Mary!
events.note: Half seven, per the ticket resellers; A.C.T. publishes no curtain times.

events.title: Iphigenia
events.note: Three performances only, on the Steindler Stage, half seven tonight. Z Space publishes nothing with dates on it until you open each show's own page, which is why this nearly went unlisted.

events.title: Julia Jacklin with Jordan Patterson
events.note: Sold out, and a second night added for Saturday. Jacklin writes about the end of things with a directness that would be unbearable if the melodies were not so good.

events.title: Julia Wolf with Bee Blackwell
events.note: Moved up from the Great American Music Hall, which is a good sign for her and a slightly worse one for the sound.

events.title: Haunted Riot with Frightwig, AroMa and Scary Story Time with Bay Curious
events.note: Frightwig were one of the founding San Francisco noise-punk bands and have barely played in years, and KQED's Bay Curious doing live ghost stories between sets is a genuinely strange and local bit of programming.

events.title: Beats & Crafts Night After Party
events.note: Free, eight o'clock, in the Lower Haight artist collective.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Eight o'clock.

events.title: Assimilation (Word for Word)
events.note: Fridays at eight.

events.title: Lady (late show)
events.note: Ten past eight.

events.title: Blade Runner: The Final Cut (35mm)
events.note: On film, which is the whole reason to go rather than watch it at home. Twenty to nine.

events.title: Frog with Mildred
events.note: Sold out. Queens duo making lo-fi Americana about the specific textures of New York, which translates better than it should.

events.title: REZN with lowheaven and Mountaineer
events.note: Chicago doom with the fuzz turned into atmosphere rather than aggression. Nine o'clock, all ages.

events.title: Petit Biscuit
events.note: Doors nine. French producer whose melodic house records are more delicate than the room usually gets.

events.title: I Heart the 90s with Josh Gelfand
events.note: Friday night at Divisadero and Fell.

events.title: Zombie Prom Costume Ball
events.note: Nine o'clock, $35, costumes assumed.

events.title: SF Neo-Futurists: The Infinite Wrench
events.note: Thirty plays in sixty minutes, order decided by the audience shouting numbers. $16 online, or $13 and the roll of a six-sided die at the door, which is the correct way to buy a ticket to this.

events.title: Bop-Nite: R&B, oldies, garage and rock'n'roll
events.note: Ten o'clock 45s night.

events.title: Cuernos: Dugi Pentagram's Birthday Celebration
events.note: The back room, ten o'clock.

events.title: Shaboozey with Angel White
events.note: The year's biggest country-rap crossover act, in a hall on Nob Hill. Angel White opens with something closer to straight Americana.

events.title: Pouya with Ramirez, Peeling Flesh, Black Smurf and Fat Nick
events.note: The Florida underground rap scene that came out of SoundCloud a decade ago, now filling the Fillmore. Peeling Flesh on the bill means this gets genuinely heavy.

events.title: SLIFT with Gumby's Junk
events.note: Toulouse trio playing psych at a volume and tempo closer to hardcore. One of the best live bands in Europe and badly under-sold here.

events.title: EAZYBAKED with R-Sun
events.note: Insomniac co-presented bass night in the main room.

events.title: First Contact: An Extraterrestrial Disco
events.note: Costumed disco in the loft, same night as the bass show downstairs.

events.title: Chief Keef
events.note: The man who more or less invented drill as a commercial form, at twenty-nine. The Midway's calendar renders client-side, so the time comes from the sweep and is not published anywhere this run could read.

events.title: LOVRA
events.note: Second room, same night.

events.title: Steam Powered Giraffe
events.note: Robot-mime musical comedy with a devoted following, in the Veterans Building. Hard to describe and not trying to be describable.

events.title: Adam Pascal
events.note: The original Roger from Rent, in cabaret. Two nights.

events.title: Victor Ruiz
events.note: Brazilian techno, late. From the sweep.

events.title: Clüb De Combat
events.note: SoMa club night; from the sweep.

events.title: Goldcap
events.note: Organic house; from the sweep.

events.title: Vicious Cycle and Here At The End
events.note: From the sweep.

events.title: Michelle Lambert
events.note: From the sweep.

events.title: Litquake: Playlist Storytellers
events.note: Writers reading to the songs that shaped them. No time confirmed — see What could not be reached.

events.title: Harvest Festival Original Art & Craft Show
events.note: Three days, several hundred makers, $9 adults. Pleasanton is in no region list in the brief; filed East Bay by proximity.

events.title: Westbrae Pumpkin Patch
events.note: Free to walk through; pumpkins $5-35. Running daily.

events.title: La maison des bois, episodes 1-3
events.note: Maurice Pialat's seven-part 1971 series about First World War foster children, shown over two afternoons. Three and a half hours today, four more tomorrow, and almost impossible to see any other way.

events.title: Friday Nights at OMCA with DATANAGAN
events.note: Five until nine, galleries open, food trucks, and DATANAGAN on the Garden Stage. Admission to the Friday Nights grounds is free; the galleries need a museum ticket. Only a handful of these left before the series stops for winter.

events.title: Halloween Market
events.note: Free entry, five o'clock, in the West Berkeley urban winery.

events.title: Hella Good Night with JWalt
events.note: Benefit for Arts for Oakland Kids. $30, six o'clock.

events.title: Basement with High Vis, Big Boy and Lowertown
events.note: Sold out, and so is Saturday. British melodic hardcore with High Vis — who are the better band — in support. Doors six, seven o'clock start, $39.50.

events.title: The Arch
events.note: Seven o'clock.

events.title: HellaSecret Speakeasy Comedy Show
events.note: Address on RSVP. Limited free tickets, otherwise discounted.

events.title: Mariachi Herencia de México: Día de los Muertos
events.note: A Chicago youth mariachi programme that grew into a Grammy-nominated touring ensemble, doing a Day of the Dead programme in Cal Performances' main hall. Mariachi at this standard in a 2,000-seat concert hall is not a thing the Bay Area gets often, and tickets start around $35. Cal Performances' own calendar would not load for this run; the time comes from the ticketing listings.

events.title: Antioch Arrow, The Pine, Allure and Nuzzle
events.note: Antioch Arrow were one of the San Diego bands that invented screamo in 1993 and they have barely existed since. All ages, volunteer-run, half seven.

events.title: Science Is a Drag: Galactic Drag Show Under the Stars
events.note: Drag performers and astronomers in the same building in the Oakland hills, telescopes open. $20, 18+.

events.title: Gary Clark Jr. with Xavier Lynn
events.note: The best electric blues guitarist of his generation playing a 2,800-seat theatre, which is roughly the right size for the sound. Doors seven.

events.title: Liberation (first preview)
events.note: Bess Wohl's play about a 1970s consciousness-raising group in a Midwestern gym, West Coast premiere, running to 29 November. First preview, eight o'clock; press night is the 28th. Berkeley Rep's own site exceeded ten redirects for this run, so the dates come from its season announcement and the times from resale listings, which disagree.

events.title: Cheekface with Bodega
events.note: Deadpan talking-over-guitars from Los Angeles, with Bodega's New York art-punk underneath. Doors eight, nine o'clock start, and the back room of a Shattuck beer hall is exactly right for it.

events.title: Diwali Festival of Lights drone show
events.note: A free drone light show over downtown Walnut Creek at quarter past nine, which is late for a family event and worth it.

events.title: Kacey Musgraves
events.note: An arena show, listed for completeness. Musgraves is the best songwriter of the three big country acts in this digest and the room is the worst of the three.

events.title: Maysa
events.note: The voice from Incognito's best records, solo. $62-89.

events.title: Los Vega
events.note: Son jarocho family band from Veracruz. They play Stanford tomorrow too; this is the cheaper night.

events.title: Pink Fuzz and The Well
events.note: Denver and Austin psych-doom on a shared bill. From the sweep; the venue's calendar fetched empty.

events.title: Chalice
events.note: Ashkenaz has been the Bay Area's world-music dance hall since 1973 and almost nothing aggregates it. From the sweep.

events.title: Celtic Thunder
events.venue: Henry J. Kaiser Center for the Arts
events.note: The Kaiser reopened as a performance hall after a long closure, and this is one of the first touring shows in it. From the sweep.

events.title: Reo Brothers
events.note: Filipino brothers' band doing sixties covers, in a 1946 San Leandro cinema. San Leandro is in no region list in the brief; filed East Bay by proximity.

events.title: Disney On Ice: Find Your Hero (morning)
events.note: Eleven o'clock, first of three shows today.

events.title: Dracula (TheatreWorks Silicon Valley), matinee
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Two o'clock.

events.title: Children's Halloween Haunt: hayrides and trick-or-treating
events.note: In the reconstructed-street museum at Kelley Park. $5.30 for adults, $10.60 for children, tickets at the gate only now.

events.title: Disney On Ice: Find Your Hero (afternoon)
events.note: Three o'clock.

events.title: Ballet of Lights: Sleeping Beauty (early show)
events.note: Projection-mapped Sleeping Beauty with live dancers, four o'clock, in the East San Jose theatre that Teatro Visión calls home.

events.title: Tunnel of Terror: Halloween makers market and lowriders
events.note: Free Halloween festival in the City Hall rotunda and plaza, with a makers market and a lowrider show. Civic programming of exactly the kind the brief says to favour.

events.title: Ballet of Lights: Sleeping Beauty (late show)
events.note: Six o'clock.

events.title: Hotel Transylvania outdoor movie night
events.note: Free, arrive half six for a half seven start. Registration required.

events.title: Disney On Ice: Find Your Hero (evening)
events.note: Seven o'clock.

events.title: Kanan Gill
events.note: Indian stand-up with a large diaspora following, playing a 3,000-seat hall in San Jose, which tells you something about where that audience is.

events.title: Blitzkid with Them Creatures
events.note: West Virginia horror-punk, reformed, a week before Halloween, which is exactly when it belongs.

events.title: Marlon Wayans (early show)
events.note: Seven o'clock.

events.title: Kellen Erskine with Ben Feldman and Nick Scarpino
events.note: Seven o'clock, earlier than the Friday show.

events.title: Mission Chamber Orchestra: Sunlight and Dance
events.note: San Jose's own chamber orchestra, and the first listing this venue has produced in four weeks — the Hammer's calendar is drawn by a widget no automated reader can see, so this came through the regional feed.

events.title: Dracula (TheatreWorks Silicon Valley)
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Half seven.

events.title: Grupo Kachimba and Sonido Inesperable

events.title: Foster City Halloween Spooktacular and Trick-or-Treat Trail
events.note: $12, eleven o'clock, on the lagoon.

events.title: Taste of Filoli Tour
events.note: One o'clock, ninety minutes, tastings included.

events.title: City of Belmont's 100th Birthday Centennial Fest, with vintage car parade and drone show
events.note: Belmont turns a hundred: a vintage car parade from Chula Vista Drive at half one, then the festival in Twin Pines Park and a drone show after dark. Free, and the only centenary in this digest.

events.title: Los Vega: Son Jarocho (early show)
events.note: A Veracruz family band playing son jarocho — requinto, jarana and a wooden platform to dance on — in a 200-seat studio. Two shows. The tradition is 300 years old and this is one of the families that carries it.

events.title: Movie Nights in the Park: The Sandlot
events.note: Free, half seven, on the coast. Bring more layers than you think.

events.title: Easy Star All-Stars: Dub Side of the Moon, with Soundclash and Andrew Diamond
events.note: The whole of Dark Side of the Moon rebuilt as roots reggae, which should be a novelty and is instead one of the better dub records of the 2000s. Doors seven.

events.title: SOFI TUKKER with DJ Drama and DRAMA
events.note: An arena booking, listed for completeness. Daly City is in no region list in the brief; filed Peninsula by proximity. 18+.

events.title: Los Vega: Son Jarocho (late show)
events.note: Nine o'clock.

events.title: Viaje Tropical with Tony Succar and Mauricio Mesones
events.note: Peruvian salsa and cumbia bill. The Fox's own page muddles the city and the ticketing is handled off-site, so the venue is from the sweep and is not fully confirmed.

events.title: Autumn Days at Filoli
events.note: The seasonal daytime run, 26 September to 1 November — the gardens at their best colour, with the house open. Nightfall, the after-dark version, runs the same window. Filoli publishes no per-day times on a page this run can read, so this is the run rather than a performance.

events.title: Free de Young Museum day for Bay Area residents
events.venue: de Young Museum, Golden Gate Park
events.note: Free to Bay Area residents with ID on the fourth Saturday, timed tickets, permanent galleries. Not confirmable on the museum's own site, which refuses every automated request — this comes from Funcheap, as it does every month.

events.title: Free Legion of Honor day for Bay Area residents
events.note: Same museum group, same free Saturday. The Miró show is up.

events.title: Free Casper (1995) screening
events.note: Free at the ten o'clock show only, in the Richmond's surviving neighbourhood cinema.

events.title: Queer History Tour: Unspeakable Vice
events.note: Two and a half hours on the city's queer history before Stonewall. Ten o'clock.

events.title: Haines Gallery: 250 Years, Indigenous Futures
events.note: On until 7 November. Haines moved onto the Fort Mason campus and the gallery is free to walk into, which is not true of most shows this good.

events.title: 44th Annual Sandcastle Classic
events.note: More than a hundred teams of architects, engineers and schoolchildren building enormous sand sculptures on Ocean Beach, free to watch, forty-fourth year. The single best free afternoon of the week, and the fog usually holds off until three.

events.title: Alemany Farm Harvest Festival
events.note: Free, eleven o'clock, on the four-and-a-half-acre volunteer farm wedged between the freeway and the Alemany projects.

events.title: BYOP Pumpkin Carving Party
events.note: Bring your own pumpkin, eleven o'clock, upper lawn. Free.

events.title: Laurel Hill Nursery School 80th Anniversary Block Party
events.note: Two blocks of Euclid closed for a nursery school's eightieth. Free, and exactly the kind of neighbourhood event that never reaches a listings site.

events.title: Walking Tour: Gold Rush and Sunken Ships
events.note: The ships buried under the Financial District. Eleven o'clock.

events.title: Walking Tour: 1906 Earthquake and Fire
events.note: Eleven o'clock.

events.title: Chowder Fest: San Francisco's best clam chowder showdown
events.note: Free to attend at Fisherman's Wharf; tasting tickets extra. Twelve o'clock.

events.title: Thrill-O-Ween: free outdoor Halloween festival
events.note: Free, midday, on the plaza outside Chase Center.

events.title: The Whale's Tail beer garden with live music
events.note: Free to enter, live bands, midday onward. Part of the park's slow conversion of its car park space into something people use.

events.title: Murals & Monuments Tour
events.note: YBCA, the library, the Arts Commission and Market Street Arts walking the mid-Market public art together. Starts at the Main Branch, half twelve, RSVP required.

events.title: SF Latino Film Festival: Comparsa
events.note: Half twelve.

events.title: San Quentin Film Festival 2026
events.note: Films made by people inside San Quentin, programmed by them. One o'clock, and the most unusual thing in any cinema this week.

events.title: Queer History Tour: Valley of the Queens
events.note: One o'clock.

events.title: Whack Donuts 2-Year Anniversary Jam and breakin' battle
events.note: Free breaking battle on the plaza, half one. Street dance in a public space is the version of this that actually works.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong (matinee)
events.note: Two o'clock.

events.title: Weekend Sessions: Afro-Filipino Jazz Project
events.note: Ninety minutes, free, outdoors, two o'clock. The Yerba Buena Gardens Festival's only date this week and the kind of cross-tradition band the festival exists to book.

events.title: Bay Beats Launch Party
events.note: Free concert at the Bandshell to launch the public library's Bay Beats streaming platform, which gives away local music for nothing — a good cause and a free afternoon in the Music Concourse.

events.title: Silent Shorts Program (Through an Open Window)
events.note: $15, including gallery admission and themed snacks. Two o'clock.

events.title: When Manilatown Swung: The Manila Serenaders
events.note: Live swing and a history of the Manilatown dance halls, in the ground floor of the rebuilt I-Hotel. Free or donation, two o'clock. The building is the story.

events.title: Walking Tour: Bar and Cocktail History
events.note: Half two, and ends somewhere useful.

events.title: Giant Sand Painting: community art on the beach
events.note: Free, registration needed, below the old Cliff House. Three o'clock, and a short walk from the sandcastles.

events.title: Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde (1931)
events.note: Afternoon repeat, three o'clock.

events.title: SF Blackout: Gambits & Ghouls chess night
events.note: Free, three o'clock, suggested $10 donation. Mission Bay.

events.title: SF Latino Film Festival: Community Voices
events.note: Shorts programme, ten past three, in Japantown.

events.title: One In A Million, with Q&A
events.note: Twenty to four, with the filmmakers afterwards.

events.title: Undiscovered SF: Filipino night market and block party
events.note: Free with an RSVP, four o'clock, SoMa — the Filipino night market that has done more for Filipino food in this city than any restaurant. Filipino American History Month, so the programming is heavier than usual.

events.title: Lit Crawl SF
events.note: Litquake's closing night and the best free four hours of the year: dozens of readings in sequence through Mission bars, bookshops and barbers from five until nine, then an afterparty. Free, $10-15 donation suggested. Pick a street rather than a programme and walk it. The full venue list could not be read — see What could not be reached.

events.title: Matinee: Lightweight Champion, Suver and Friday Harbor
events.note: Five o'clock, Seattle headliner.

events.note: Quarter past five.

events.title: Terror Vault: 1874 Halloween Haunt

events.title: Making Marie Antoinette
events.note: The companion documentary to Friday's restoration. Twenty-five to seven.

events.title: Golden Gate Comedy Night
events.note: Free with RSVP, 21+.

events.title: Crazy Funny Asians comedy showcase
events.note: Free with RSVP, $5-10 donation suggested, $25 at the door. One of the longest-running Asian American comedy showcases in the country.

events.title: Hisaishi Conducts Hisaishi
events.note: Third and last night. See Thursday.

events.title: Manon (San Francisco Opera)
events.note: Third of four remaining performances, half seven. From $30.

events.title: illuminati hotties with Buzzed Lightbeer, Satana Satana and Swell Foop
events.note: Sarah Tudzin writes the best-produced guitar pop in Los Angeles and plays it like a punk band. Doors seven, half seven start, $27-30, and three local supports for that price.

events.title: The Maraschinos, Stay Out, Addalemon and Hell Bound Pound

events.title: Assimilation (Word for Word)

events.title: Full Moon Trip Temple
events.note: Free, donations appreciated, eight o'clock in a Grant Avenue storefront gallery. Exactly the kind of North Beach thing the brief's talks-and-oddities bucket exists for.

events.title: The Confessional
events.note: Improv built from audience confessions. Eight o'clock, $11.94.

events.title: Puff Puff Laugh
events.note: Comedy in a cannabis lounge, free with RSVP, 21+, one-item minimum.

events.title: K.Flay with Yogurt
events.note: Second of two nights; the Friday is sold out. K.Flay came out of Stanford and the Bay Area rap scene before she went pop-punk, so a 350-cap Potrero room is a homecoming of sorts. Doors half seven, all ages, $30.

events.title: Everclear with American Hi-Fi
events.note: Two nights in the region: a 500-cap club tonight and a hillside winery tomorrow. The club is the one to take.

events.title: Weatherday with Founders Day and hit me, Harold!
events.note: Swedish bedroom emo recorded at a volume that breaks the microphones, played loud in a converted mortuary chapel. Nine o'clock, $25-30.

events.title: she's green
events.note: Nine o'clock, all ages, $36.22.

events.title: Tinzo + Jojo: Dark Library Tour
events.note: First of two shows, doors nine.

events.title: Let's Go Disco and Garage O'Clock Rock
events.note: Two rooms, two records policies, one bar.

events.title: SF Neo-Futurists: The Infinite Wrench
events.note: Nine o'clock. Different order, different plays.

events.title: Your F***ed Up Relationship
events.note: Nine o'clock, $16.37.

events.title: HellaSecret Desi Comedy Night
events.note: Free for the first hundred RSVPs, $25 at the door, address on booking.

events.title: Music for Families
events.note: The orchestra's family matinee series. No time is published on any page this run could read — the Symphony's calendar sits behind a queueing redirect — so confirm before setting out.

events.title: Marc Rebillet with Chromeo and Franc Moody
events.note: Rebillet improvises entire funk songs from a loop pedal in a dressing gown, and Chromeo on the same bill makes this the most purely enjoyable dance ticket of the week. From the sweep; the Midway publishes no times a reader can see.

events.title: Tokyo Machine
events.note: Second room.

events.title: Jodeci
events.note: The group that took gospel harmony into early-nineties R&B and made it filthy. They tour rarely and badly, and when it works it is extraordinary.

events.title: Amble with Vincent Lima
events.note: Irish three-part-harmony folk act who have gone from busking to the Fillmore in about three years.

events.title: Jai Wolf with Koastle
events.note: Melodic electronic with a live band, in a ballroom with a sprung floor.

events.title: Protomartyr with Accessory
events.note: Second Bay Area night after San Jose. If you only go to one post-punk show this week, go to this one — Casey's writing about the collapse of an industrial city is the best lyric writing in American guitar music.

events.title: Ivy Lab: A Farewell Tour, with Great Dane, DJ Dials and Mr. Carmack
events.note: The last Ivy Lab tour, with Mr. Carmack on the bill, which makes this the best line-up Public Works has had in months.

events.title: Kelsey Kindall with Kailnoa
events.note: Basement bill.

events.title: Tyondai Braxton with Matt Robidoux
events.note: Braxton left Battles to write music for orchestras and modular synthesisers and has been making the most structurally interesting electronic records in America since. The Lab is the right room: a hundred people, concrete, no stage.

events.title: Ghoul with Dry Socket, Surprise Privilege and Vile Rites
events.note: Oakland's costumed thrash band in the reopened Mabuhay Gardens, which was the city's punk club from 1976 to 1986 and is operating again. From the sweep.

events.title: Lucas Zelnick (early show)
events.note: Two stand-up shows in the Palace theatre.

events.title: Lucas Zelnick (late show)
events.note: Second show.

events.title: Adam Pascal
events.note: Second night.

events.title: Konstantin Sibold
events.note: Stuttgart house, late. From the sweep.

events.title: BATS Improv
events.note: Long-form improv in the Fort Mason loft, running most Saturdays through the end of the year. Fort Mason's calendar carries the date but no time.

events.title: Every Saturday Night (A.C.T. ACTivate)
events.note: A.C.T.'s ACTivate strand, running 10 October to 1 November at the Strand. The title names the night; A.C.T. publishes no curtain times anywhere on its site, so the day is confirmed and the hour is not.

events.title: Paramount Theatre public tour
events.note: Two hours inside the best art deco interior on the West Coast for ten dollars, card only. The theatre is otherwise dark until the 30th, so this is the only way in this week.

events.title: 18th Annual Halloween / Pumpkin Festival
events.note: Free admission to a Halloween festival in an Olmsted-designed cemetery, which is either the most or the least appropriate setting possible. Midday.

events.title: West Oakland Prescott Craft Market
events.note: Fifty-plus vendors and DJs, free, midday.

events.title: Tricks, Treats & Traditions in The Laurel
events.note: Free Halloween and Day of the Dead street event on MacArthur. Midday.

events.title: Howl-O-Ween with dog runway and adoptions
events.note: Free, one o'clock, costumed dogs. RSVP encouraged.

events.title: La maison des bois, episodes 4-7
events.note: Four more hours of Pialat, two o'clock. Together with Friday this is the whole series.

events.title: RADwood NorCal: Bay Area '80s and '90s car festival
events.note: Free with online registration, four o'clock, in an aircraft hangar on the old naval air station. Period dress encouraged and widely honoured.

events.title: Filipino American History Month Fest with DJs and pop-up tattoos
events.note: $8.88 early bird, rising to $18.88 at the door. Five o'clock in the West Oakland beer garden.

events.title: Hike & Sip: Halloween Hike
events.note: $40, 21+, five o'clock, in the hills above the observatory.

events.title: Basement with High Vis, Big Boy and Lowertown
events.note: Second night, also sold out. Doors six.

events.title: Bear Ghost with Sarah and the Safe Word and Spaceman Bob
events.note: Theatrical Arizona rock, doors six, seven o'clock start.

events.title: Le petit soldat
events.note: Godard's second feature, banned in France for three years over Algeria. Seven o'clock.

events.title: Oakland Comedy Saturday Night at a secret speakeasy
events.note: Two shows, seven and nine. Free with the code, limited.

events.title: Christian Sands Trio
events.note: One of the best jazz pianists under forty, playing the early set in a room built for it. $34-49, half seven.

events.title: Ho99o9 and N8NOFACE with Sincerely___ The Void
events.note: Industrial hip-hop and synth-punk in an all-ages volunteer-run warehouse, which is a better venue for both than any club would be. Half seven.

events.title: William Black with Vincent, Afinity and IKU
events.note: Melodic bass in a 2,800-seat theatre. Doors seven.

events.title: Haunted USS Hornet Monster Bash with Bowie tribute band
events.note: A costume party on the hangar deck of an aircraft carrier that recovered the Apollo 11 crew and is widely held to be haunted. $40, eight o'clock.

events.title: Buttah's Jook Joint
events.note: Late R&B revue, half nine, $45.

events.title: Liberation (preview)
events.note: Second preview. No time could be confirmed; see the Friday listing for why.

events.title: John Gorka
events.note: Thirty-five years of the fastidiously written American folk song, in the room that most suits it.

events.title: The Recyclists with Lucky Drive and Duty Free
events.note: Local power-pop bill in the Albany dive.

events.title: Mistah F.A.B.
events.note: Hyphy institution and North Oakland community figure. From the sweep.

events.title: Super Diamond
events.note: The long-running San Francisco Neil Diamond tribute, which is a genuine Bay Area institution and, per the brief, listed and not featured.

events.title: Al Jardine
events.note: A founding Beach Boy, solo, in Livermore. The city is in no region list in the brief; filed East Bay by proximity.

events.title: Gabby Concepcion
events.note: Filipino screen star, live. From the sweep.

events.title: Halloween Trick-or-Treat Trail
events.note: In the gardens of the house Sarah Winchester kept building for thirty-eight years, which needs no extra Halloween decoration. $16.09 children, $5.37 adults, ten o'clock.

events.title: Nekromantix with Rezurex
events.note: Psychobilly, upright coffin bass included, seven o'clock. Second horror-punk booking of the weekend at this room.

events.title: Disney On Ice: Find Your Hero
events.note: Closing day of the arena run. The Saturday schedule suggests more than one show; only the run's dates are published.

events.title: Everclear with American Hi-Fi
events.note: The hillside version of Saturday's club show, and the colder one.

events.title: Marlon Wayans
events.note: Last of the weekend's five shows.

events.title: Destino Perdido
events.note: From the sweep.

events.title: Costumed Witch Paddle
events.note: Several hundred people in witch costume on kayaks and paddleboards in a sheltered harbour. Free if you have a boat, rentals extra, life vest required. Ten o'clock, and genuinely one of the best photographs of the year.

events.title: Upstairs Downstairs Tour
events.note: Ninety minutes through the service wing as well as the state rooms, which is the more interesting half of any great house. Eleven o'clock.

events.title: Rob Kapilow: What Makes It Great? The Music of Lerner and Loewe
events.note: Kapilow takes a piece apart at the piano and then plays it whole, and he is very good at making an audience hear structure. Half two.

events.title: Grex live on KFJC
events.note: The Oakland art-rock duo playing live on the Foothill College station, which broadcasts the kind of thing nobody else will. Free to listen; the studio audience is small.

events.title: Spirit + Sound
events.note: From the sweep.

events.title: Fort Mason Center Farmers Market
events.note: Sundays, half nine to half one, on the pier apron with the Golden Gate behind it.

events.title: SFMOMA Free Family Day
events.note: Up to four adults free per visitor aged eighteen or under, from ten. The cheapest way a family gets into this building all year.

events.title: Try lawn bowling at the historic club in Golden Gate Park
events.note: The oldest public lawn bowling club in the United States, free instruction, flat shoes required. Ten o'clock, and exactly the sort of thing the brief's oddities bucket is for.

events.title: World of Dumplings
events.note: Free to enter, eleven until five, with dumpling makers from a dozen traditions in the nave of the Ferry Building. Food costs money; the queueing is the event.

events.title: Lindy in the Park
events.note: Free swing dancing on closed roadway, eleven until two, every Sunday since 1995. Cancelled if it rains.

events.title: Bark at Spark: Howl-O-Ween
events.note: Free, eleven o'clock, costumed dogs in Mission Bay.

events.title: SF Music Day 2026
events.note: More than twenty free concerts across four halls of the Veterans Building in one afternoon, from midday — chamber music, jazz, new music, world traditions, running continuously so you can walk between them. InterMusic SF have done this for nineteen years and it remains the single best free music day in the city.

events.title: Wiggle Fest Fall 2026 block party
events.note: Free block party on the bike-route plaza at Duboce and Steiner. Midday.

events.title: Sundays at the Beach free yoga day
events.note: Free yoga on the closed stretch of the Great Highway, midday. The promenade's best argument for itself.

events.title: Blue Bear School of Music All Star Band Fall Showcase
events.note: Free, one o'clock, all ages. Blue Bear has taught adults and children to play in bands in this city since 1971 and this is the end-of-term gig. One of only a handful of free club shows in the digest.

events.title: Tell Me Tell Me, Wave Wise and Loser Soup
events.note: A one o'clock Sunday matinee, three bands. Nothing else in the city programmes like this.

events.title: Golden Gate Park Sunday Roller Disco
events.note: Free, one o'clock, the sound system that has been there since the seventies. Bring skates.

events.title: Oh, Mary! (matinee)
events.note: One o'clock, per the resellers.

events.title: Playing with Fire: An Ecosexual Emergency
events.note: With an introduction and a Q&A. One o'clock.

events.title: SF Latino Film Festival: Libertad
events.note: One o'clock.

events.title: Orchestre Symphonique de Montréal, Rafael Payare and Leonidas Kavakos
events.note: Payare's Montreal orchestra on its California tour, with Kavakos playing the Tchaikovsky concerto and Shostakovich's Tenth after the interval. Two o'clock. The Shostakovich is the reason to go: Payare conducts it as the political document it is, and this orchestra's strings are among the best on the continent. The second unmissable thing at Davies in four days.

events.title: Tinzo + Jojo: Dark Library Tour (second show)
events.note: A two o'clock matinee version, doors at two, which is an unusual thing for this room to do.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Two o'clock, and the last performance of the week.

events.title: Assimilation (Word for Word)
events.note: Sundays at two.

events.title: Iphigenia
events.note: Closing performance, two o'clock, Steindler Stage.

events.note: Three o'clock.

events.note: The Painted Ladies block closed for trick-or-treating, four o'clock, free.

events.note: Ten past five.

events.title: The 90s Simpsons Trivia Happy Hour
events.note: Six o'clock. The venue's ticketing widget lists it twice under two links; it is one night.

events.title: Thick & Tired drag show and Sunday B3 Sessions
events.note: Drag in the early evening, then the Hammond organ night that has run on Sundays here for years.

events.title: NAZA
events.note: Six o'clock.

events.title: Oh, Mary!
events.note: Half six, per the resellers.

events.title: Joy Oladokun with Madeline Edwards
events.note: Doors six, seven o'clock start — early for the Castro. Oladokun writes plainly about faith and being Black and queer in Nashville, and the songs are better for refusing to be anthems.

events.title: Ronnie Blaze, Bromf and Whalebone FM
events.note: Seven o'clock.

events.title: S.F. Comedy Showcase
events.note: The Sunday showcase, running since 1979, with free guest-list places if you RSVP. Seven o'clock, two-drink minimum.

events.title: Sunday Comedy Night
events.note: Free with RSVP.

events.title: Perdita Durango
events.note: Álex de la Iglesia's 1997 film, which is as unpleasant and as alive as anything in the Gialloween orbit. Twenty past seven.

events.title: BALTHVS with Slow Coast
events.note: Bogotá trio playing psychedelic cumbia with Anatolian guitar tone, which is a more coherent combination than it sounds. Eight o'clock.

events.title: Kyle Gordon
events.note: The comedian behind the viral fake-genre songs, doing them live. Eight o'clock, $25-30, all ages.

events.title: The History of Concrete
events.note: Eight o'clock, last of the week.

events.title: Castle record release, with Nite and Three Towers
events.note: Bay Area doom-metal duo launching a record. Doors eight, 21+, $15 advance. The club closes for good at the end of 2026, which makes every remaining night here worth taking.

events.title: Reggae Sunday: Strictly Rockers
events.note: Nine o'clock, roots and rockers 45s.

events.title: Doja Cat
events.note: The biggest ticket of the week and an arena, so: listed, not featured. Findable without help.

events.title: Kishi Bashi with Geographer
events.note: Violin, loop pedal and an unembarrassed sense of wonder. Geographer are a San Francisco band of long standing and the pairing makes sense.

events.title: Blessing Offor
events.note: Nigerian-American soul singer, blind since childhood, with a gospel-pop catalogue that has grown steadily.

events.title: Resavoir
events.note: Will Miller's Chicago jazz project, playing the Richmond cinema's live-music configuration. The sweep lists this twice under two spellings; it is one show.

events.title: Villem
events.note: Drum and bass on Folsom. From the sweep.

events.title: Smush with Sofia, Afterglow and Brother M.
events.note: From the sweep.

events.title: Ira Wolf with Noah Solt
events.note: Montana songwriter in a fifty-seat room.

events.title: Last Minet
events.note: From the sweep.

events.title: Lucas Zelnick (early show)
events.note: Two more shows after Saturday's pair.

events.title: Lucas Zelnick (late show)
events.note: Second show.

events.title: Free Halloween trick-or-treating and haunted hunt
events.note: Free, ten o'clock, through the Montclair shops.

events.title: 32nd Annual Día de los Muertos Community Celebration
events.note: Thirty-second year: ofrendas, Aztec dance, printmaking and food across the whole museum campus, eleven until four, $10. The longest-running institutional Day of the Dead programme in the region and much the best value.

events.title: 34th Annual Rockridge Halloween Parade
events.note: Free, all ages, eleven o'clock, down College Avenue. Thirty-fourth year and still entirely run by the neighbourhood.

events.title: Oakland Bicycle Scavenger Hunt and Scaredy Cat Race
events.note: $13, eleven o'clock, by Lake Merritt.

events.title: Free Oakland Up Market
events.note: A free market in the literal sense: take one indoor item per person, donate for more. Midday.

events.title: Gallery chat with traditional medicine practitioner Batul True Heart
events.note: Forty-five minutes in the Natural Sciences gallery, one o'clock, included with the $10 festival admission.

events.title: The Rubinoos
events.note: Berkeley power-pop since 1970, playing a two o'clock matinee.

events.title: Hardcore For Pits West Benefit
events.note: A two o'clock all-ages benefit matinee.

events.title: Howl-O-Ween costumed pet parade
events.note: Free, two o'clock. San Ramon is in no region list in the brief; filed East Bay by proximity.

events.title: Future of Piano: 2026/27 season opening concert
events.note: Season opener in a 1911 clubhouse that seats about a hundred, $17.85 with the discount code, and the livestream is free. Three o'clock.

events.title: Colorful Youth
events.note: Four o'clock.

events.note: Free with RSVP, six o'clock.

events.title: Katie Cash with The Queen & I and Build A Rocket
events.note: Half six, after the matinee.

events.title: Marion Meadows
events.note: Smooth jazz saxophone, seven o'clock, $39-89.

events.title: After Hours
events.note: Seven o'clock.

events.title: Black Flag
events.note: Greg Ginn's current Black Flag in the back room of a Shattuck beer hall, doors seven. Whatever you make of the line-up, the songs are the foundation of American hardcore and this is a 300-capacity room, which is where they were written to be played. They played Felton on Friday; Berkeley is the one to take.

events.title: Liberation (preview)
events.note: Third preview. No time could be confirmed.

events.title: The Freight's One Song All Night: Fleetwood Mac's Dreams
events.note: A dozen Bay Area acts each playing the same song in their own idiom, all night. Terrence Brewer, Rip Room and Adrienne Shamszad among them. Sounds like an endurance test and is actually the most fun idea in the region's music programming.

events.title: Semuta, Trough and Feefawfum
events.note: From the sweep.

events.title: Ben Goldberg with Hamir Atwal
events.note: Goldberg's clarinet is one of the defining sounds of Bay Area improvised music, in a Maybeck-designed house in the Berkeley hills that seats about forty. From the sweep.

events.title: Eric Idle in conversation with Dave Eggers
events.note: Idle is eighty-three and does not tour, and Eggers is an unusually good interviewer when he is interested. $45, four o'clock, at Dominican University. This is the only other thing north or south of the region that clears the brief's bar for the drive this week.
